newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 29.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 29.

text.p: --------------GAM-------------------- REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -----------May 29, 1997----------------- News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends *********************************************** ADVERTISING & MARKETING: FRANKFURT - Springer & Jacoby executives Frank Blauth, Andreas Lehmann and Stefan Trocha have left with the account from Virgin Interactive Entertainment in hand and founded a new agency, Adquarter. (Horizont) ********* WALLDORF - Private station Sat1 has said it will stop broadcasting the Game of the Week from Austria soccer's Bundesliga next season, but will still feature some Austrian matches. General manager Jueger Doetz explained the decision by saying it was senseless to show the Game of the Week when digital pay-TV package DF1 was also carrying it. During the season 1997-98, only DF1's sports channel DSF will carry Austrian top games. (Kress) *********************************************** MEDIA & THE INTERNET: MUNICH - Television company ProSieben Media AG says it has signed a deal with Hollywood studio DreamWorks Productions for the rights to 86 films and several television series. ProSieben says it has signed an agreement with DreamWorks, owned by Steven Spielberg, former Disney chief executive Jeffrey Katzenberg and producer David Geffen. No financial terms were made available. (Reuter) ********* BERLIN - Television station Puls-TV says it has declared bankruptcy, two weeks after its investors pulled funding on the ailing channel. But the small regional network, which has focused on Berlin and the surrounding state of Brandenburg and was formerly known as 1A, said it would continue broadcasting reruns of programming as long as possible. (Reuter) ********* BERLIN - The heads of German public broadcasting network ARD and private stations' lobby (VPRT) battle publicly over whether two new public stations can receive viewer fees. The European Commission will decide in mid-June if the German channels Phoenix and the Kinderkanal, run jointly by public networks ARD and ZDF, are also eligible to receive state-mandated fees that the two networks obtain. (Reuter) ********* BERLIN - The Internet industry's growth is slowing after its initial boom, now more focused on trade between businesses and less on individual users, market analysts say. Online shopping has also failed to take off the way investors had hoped, largely because many consumers in Germany do not trust the new technology the way Americans do. (Die Zeit) *********************************************** BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS: BONN - Postal minister Wolfgang Boetsch says the government is considering plans to quickly sell its stake in Deutsche Telekom AG. Boetsch tells a news conference in Bonn that the government, which holds a 74 percent stake, was looking at different ways to further privatise Telekom including "unloading the whole package" on a strategic partner. (Reuter) ********* FRANKFURT - Sportswear maker adidas AG says it is confident of beating its 1996 record results this year and expressed interest in reviewing share buyback plans and raising its future dividend payouts. Adidas Chief Executive Robert Louis-Dreyfus, announcing he also wanted to stay on at the helm of the company through the turn of the century, said the group would meet the expectations of investors with its 1997 results. (Reuter) ********* MUNICH - Insurance giant Allianz AG Holding says it has not yet identified a single valid claim against it relating to insurance policies sold to victims of Nazi persecution. The company has launched a major campaign to help relatives of Holocaust victims track down missing assets after it was named with six other insurers in a class action suit launched earlier this year in the U.S. (Reuter) *********************************************** PEOPLE NEWS: WALLDORF - Martina Rudy will take up the directorship Volkswagen AG's new Team Technik- and Kulturkommunikation, effective October 1. She leaves packing manufacturer Schmalbach Lubeca of the Viag Group for the new position. (Kress)
